title: Federal-local conflict over immigration enforcement and troops (2025-2026)
text: Since June 2025, immigration enforcement has been the sharpest line of conflict between federal and local government in Los Angeles. Raids starting June 6, 2025 set off protests; the President federalized about 4,000 California Guard members and sent about 700 Marines over the Governor's objection. California sued (Newsom v. Trump), and a federal judge later found the deployment violated the Posse Comitatus Act and ordered it ended; it ended on Dec 31, 2025. ICE arrests in the LA area more than tripled in 2025 to more than 14,000, then fell sharply in early 2026. City and state sanctuary laws keep LAPD and the Sheriff out of civil immigration enforcement, which DHS leadership continues to criticize. Sources: Wikipedia (Newsom v. Trump); LAist; ABC7; California Insider.

title: Who secures LA28: the layered security structure
text: The 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games are a National Special Security Event, so the US Secret Service leads security planning and coordinates LAPD, the Sheriff, CHP and city police in venue cities such as Inglewood and Pasadena. A White House task force created by executive order on Aug 5, 2025 and chaired by the President coordinates security, visas and transportation, backed by $1 billion in federal funding. The President has said the Guard or military could be used. Local leaders, including Pasadena's mayor, want local police to lead day-to-day safety. Sources: LAist; ABC7; Spectrum News 1.

title: Wildfire recovery money: how aid flows from Washington to Palisades and Altadena
text: Recovery money after the January 2025 fires moves through several layers. The President approves disaster declarations; FEMA (inside DHS) pays individual housing aid and reimburses public rebuilding; Cal OES coordinates for the state; the City (Palisades) and the County (Altadena) run rebuilding and permits. California asked Congress for $33.9 billion; about $5.7 billion in FEMA aid had arrived by late 2025. FEMA extended housing aid for homeowners to July 9, 2027 but for renters only to Oct 9, 2026, and paused non-emergency recovery work during the 2026 DHS funding lapse. Sources: ABC7; NBC Los Angeles; Hoodline; Claims Journal.

title: November 3, 2026: elections that could change who governs LA
text: Several bodies that shape life in LA have elections on Nov 3, 2026. The Mayor's race is a runoff between incumbent Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman, with the winner taking office Dec 14. Eight of 15 City Council seats are on the ballot. The County Sheriff's race is a rematch between Robert Luna and Alex Villanueva. The governor's race is Democrat Xavier Becerra vs Republican Steve Hilton, replacing term-limited Gavin Newsom in January 2027. Neighboring Nevada and Arizona also elect governors. Until results are certified, agents should treat current office-holders as in charge. Sources: ABC7; LAist; GV Wire; Wikipedia.

title: Layers of government a Los Angeles resident lives under
text: A resident of the City of LA is governed by several layers at once. The City (Mayor, Council, LAPD, LAFD, LADWP) sets local law such as rent and wage rules. The County (Board of Supervisors, Sheriff, Public Health) runs health, social services, jails and courts support. LAUSD and LACCD are separate governments for schools and colleges, and Metro and LAHSA are regional or joint bodies. The State can preempt local rules and commands the Guard; the federal government enforces immigration law, funds disaster recovery and leads security for events like LA28. Separate cities such as San Fernando, Santa Monica and Inglewood sit inside or beside LA with their own rules. Sources: EmpowerLA; Wikipedia (Board of Supervisors); Wikipedia (Newsom v. Trump).

title: Los Angeles Neighborhood Councils (EmpowerLA) (neighborhood-level body)
text: Los Angeles Neighborhood Councils (EmpowerLA) is a neighborhood-level body (advisory). Jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles, 99 neighborhood council areas of about 40,000 people each. title: Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors (Los Angeles County body)

title: Consulate General of Mexico in Los Angeles (foreign diplomatic mission)
text: Consulate General of Mexico in Los Angeles is a foreign diplomatic mission (diplomatic), part of United Mexican States (Government of Mexico). Jurisdiction: Consular district covering Los Angeles County's 88 cities. Purpose: provide documents, legal help and protection to Mexican nationals in LA County. Led by Consul General Carlos González Gutiérrez (since February 2024), appointed. title: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (US federal body)
text: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement is a US federal body (law enforcement), part of US Department of Homeland Security. Jurisdiction: United States; LA Area of Responsibility covers seven Southern California counties. Purpose: arrest, detain and deport people for civil immigration violations. Led by Field Office Director (LA) Thomas Giles, career. ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations arrests and detains noncitizens. ICE arrests in the LA area more than tripled in 2025 to more than 14,000, peaking in June 2025, then fell sharply in early 2026.
